label: hartshorne algebraic geometry, pp. 10-20
title: hartshorne algebraic geometry
preamble:
import Mathlib
import Lean4All.Definitions.SrcHartsAg
open SrcHartsAg
conventions: Use `Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineSpace` or `Fin n → k` for affine space $\mathbf{A}^n$ over a field $k$.
Use `Ideal k` for ideals in the polynomial ring $A = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$.
Use `Set (Fin n → k)` for subsets of affine space.
Define `Z (T : Set (Ideal k))` as the set of common zeros of the ideal generated by $T$, or more commonly `V (I : Ideal k)` for the vanishing set of an ideal $I$.
Use `IsAlgebraicSet` or a predicate `IsZariskiClosed` to denote algebraic sets (closed sets in the Zariski topology).
The Zariski topology is defined via `TopologicalSpace` instance on `Fin n → k` where closed sets are algebraic sets.
Use `I (Y : Set (Fin n → k))` for the ideal of polynomials vanishing on $Y$.
Assume `k` is a field (`Field k`) unless specified otherwise (e.g., algebraically closed for Nullstellensatz).
conventions_ko: 체 $k$ 위의 아핀 공간 $\mathbf{A}^n$은 `Fin n → k` 또는 `Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineSpace`로 표현한다.
다항식 환 $A = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$의 아이디얼은 `Ideal k`를 사용한다.
아핀 공간의 부분집합은 `Set (Fin n → k)`를 사용한다.
아이디얼 $I$의 영점 집합은 `V I`로, 집합 $T$의 영점 집합은 `Z T`로 정의한다.
대수적 집합(자리스키 위상의 닫힌 집합)은 `IsAlgebraicSet` 또는 `IsZariskiClosed` 술어로 나타낸다.
자리스키 위상은 `Fin n → k` 위에 닫힌 집합이 대수적 집합인 `TopologicalSpace` 인스턴스로 정의한다.
특이 명시되지 않는 한 $k$는 체(`Field k`)라고 가정한다.
definitions:
import Mathlib

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace SrcHartsAg

/-- The vanishing set $Z(T)$ of a subset $T$ of the polynomial ring $A = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$. It is the set of points $P \in \mathbf{A}^n$ such that $f(P) = 0$ for all $f \in T$. -/
def vanishingSet {k : Type*} [Field k] {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (T : Set (MvPolynomial n k)) : Set (n → k) :=
  { P | ∀ f ∈ T, MvPolynomial.eval P f = 0 }

/-- A subset $Y$ of $\mathbf{A}^n$ is an algebraic set if there exists a subset $T$ of the polynomial ring $A$ such that $Y = Z(T)$. -/
def algebraicSet {k : Type*} [Field k] {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (Y : Set (n → k)) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : Set (MvPolynomial n k), Y = vanishingSet T

end SrcHartsAg

items.name: Algebraic Set
items.tex: A subset $Y$ of $\mathbf{A}^n$ is an \textit{algebraic set} if there exists a subset $T \subseteq A$ such that $Y = Z(T)$.
The union of two algebraic sets is an algebraic set. The intersection of any family of algebraic sets is an algebraic set. The empty set and the whole space are algebraic sets.
items.statement_en: Let $k$ be a field and $n$ be a finite type. The collection of algebraic sets in $\mathbf{A}^n_k$ satisfies the axioms of closed sets for a topology: the union of two algebraic sets is an algebraic set, the intersection of any family of algebraic sets is an algebraic set, and both the empty set and the whole space are algebraic sets.
items.statement_ko: $k$를 체, $n$을 유한 타입이라고 하자. $\mathbf{A}^n_k$의 대수적 집합들의 모임은 위상의 닫힌 집합 공리를 만족한다: 두 대수적 집합의 합집합은 대수적 집합이고, 임의의 대수적 집합들의 교집합은 대수적 집합이며, 공집합과 전체 공간 모두 대수적 집합이다.
items.lean: (k : Type*) [Field k] (n : Type*) [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] : (∀ Y₁ Y₂ : Set (n → k), algebraicSet Y₁ → algebraicSet Y₂ → algebraicSet (Y₁ ∪ Y₂)) ∧ (∀ (ι : Type*) (Y : ι → Set (n → k)), (∀ i, algebraicSet (Y i)) → algebraicSet (⋂ i, Y i)) ∧ algebraicSet (∅ : Set (n → k)) ∧ algebraicSet (Set.univ : Set (n → k))
items.note: The previous error was due to Lean not being able to infer the type for `DecidableEq` in the context of `algebraicSet ∅` and `algebraicSet Set.univ` without explicit type annotations. Adding `(∅ : Set (n → k))` and `(Set.univ : Set (n → k))` resolves the metavariable issue.

items.name: Zariski topology
items.tex: We define the *Zariski topology* on $\mathbf{A}^n$ by taking the open subsets to be the complements of the algebraic sets. This is a topology, because according to the proposition, the intersection of two open sets is open, and the union of any family of open sets is open. Furthermore, the empty set and the whole space are both open.

Let us consider the Zariski topology on the affine line $\mathbf{A}^1$. Every ideal in $A = k[x]$ is principal, so every algebraic set is the set of zeros of a single polynomial. Since $k$ is algebraically closed, every nonzero polynomial $f(x)$ can be written $f(x) = c(x - a_1) \cdots (x - a_n)$ with $c, a_1, \ldots, a_n \in k$. Then $Z(f) = \{a_1, \ldots, a_n\}$. Thus the algebraic sets in $\mathbf{A}^1$ are just the finite subsets (including the empty set) and the whole space (corresponding to $f = 0$). Thus the open sets are the empty set and the complements of finite subsets. Notice in particular that this topology is not Hausdorff.
$\mathbf{A}^1$ is irreducible, because its only proper closed subsets are finite, yet it is infinite (because $k$ is algebraically closed, hence infinite).
Any nonempty open subset of an irreducible space is irreducible and dense.
If $Y$ is an irreducible subset of $X$, then its closure $\overline{Y}$ in $X$ is also irreducible.

(a) If $T_1 \subseteq T_2$ are subsets of $A$, then $Z(T_1) \supseteq Z(T_2)$.
(b) If $Y_1 \subseteq Y_2$ are subsets of $\mathbf{A}^n$, then $I(Y_1) \supseteq I(Y_2)$.
(c) For any two subsets $Y_1, Y_2$ of $\mathbf{A}^n$, we have $I(Y_1 \cup Y_2) = I(Y_1) \cap I(Y_2)$.
(d) For any ideal $\mathfrak{a} \subseteq A$, $I(Z(\mathfrak{a})) = \sqrt{\mathfrak{a}}$, the radical of $\mathfrak{a}$.
(e) For any subset $Y \subseteq \mathbf{A}^n$, $Z(I(Y)) = \overline{Y}$, the closure of $Y$.
items.title_en: Basic properties of the vanishing set and ideal operators
items.title_ko: 소멸 집합과 아이디얼 연산자의 기본 성질
items.statement_en:
Let $k$ be a field and $n$ be a finite type. Let $A = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be the polynomial ring. For subsets $T_1, T_2 \subseteq A$ and $Y_1, Y_2 \subseteq \mathbf{A}^n$:
(a) If $T_1 \subseteq T_2$, then $Z(T_1) \supseteq Z(T_2)$.
(b) If $Y_1 \subseteq Y_2$, then $I(Y_1) \supseteq I(Y_2)$.
(c) $I(Y_1 \cup Y_2) = I(Y_1) \cap I(Y_2)$.
(d) For any ideal $\mathfrak{a} \subseteq A$, $I(Z(\mathfrak{a})) = \sqrt{\mathfrak{a}}$.
(e) For any subset $Y \subseteq \mathbf{A}^n$, $Z(I(Y)) = \overline{Y}$.
items.statement_ko:
$k$를 체, $n$을 유한 타입이라고 하자. $A = k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$을 다항식 환이라고 하자. 부분집합 $T_1, T_2 \subseteq A$와 $Y_1, Y_2 \subseteq \mathbf{A}^n$에 대하여:
(a) $T_1 \subseteq T_2$이면 $Z(T_1) \supseteq Z(T_2)$이다.
(b) $Y_1 \subseteq Y_2$이면 $I(Y_1) \supseteq I(Y_2)$이다.
(c) $I(Y_1 \cup Y_2) = I(Y_1) \cap I(Y_2)$이다.
(d) 임의의 아이디얼 $\mathfrak{a} \subseteq A$에 대하여 $I(Z(\mathfrak{a})) = \sqrt{\mathfrak{a}}$이다.
(e) 임의의 부분집합 $Y \subseteq \mathbf{A}^n$에 대하여 $Z(I(Y)) = \overline{Y}$이다.
items.lean: (k : Type*) [Field k] (n : Type*) [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (T₁ T₂ : Set (MvPolynomial n k)) (Y₁ Y₂ : Set (n → k)) : (T₁ ⊆ T₂ → vanishingSet T₂ ⊆ vanishingSet T₁) ∧ (Y₁ ⊆ Y₂ → vanishingSet (Set.image (fun f => f) Y₁) ⊆ vanishingSet (Set.image (fun f => f) Y₂)) ∧ (vanishingSet (Set.image (fun f => f) (Y₁ ∪ Y₂)) = vanishingSet (Set.image (fun f => f) Y₁) ∩ vanishingSet (Set.image (fun f => f) Y₂)) ∧ (∀ (a : Ideal (MvPolynomial n k)), vanishingSet (a : Set (MvPolynomial n k)) = vanishingSet (a.radical : Set (MvPolynomial n k))) ∧ (∀ (Y : Set (n → k)), vanishingSet (Set.image (fun f => f) Y) = closure Y)
items.note: Not formalizable yet. The shared definitions provided only include `vanishingSet` (Z). The operator $I(Y)$ (the ideal of polynomials vanishing on Y) is not defined in the shared namespace. Furthermore, part (d) requires the Nullstellensatz (specifically that $k$ is algebraically closed) to hold, which is not stated in the general hypotheses of the proposition in the prompt (though often assumed in this context). Part (e) requires the definition of the Zariski topology on affine space to define the closure $\overline{Y}$. Without definitions for $I(Y)$ and the Zariski topology, and without the algebraically closed assumption for (d), the statement cannot be faithfully formalized using only the provided shared definitions.
